signal: XOi launched Advisor, an AI-driven asset intelligence solution, and acquired Specifx (Jan 2025)

email.body1:
Brandon, saw XOi launched Advisor and folded in the Specifx acquisition.

Moves like that open more field-service accounts than the team can personally cover before they cool off. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for XOi off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Brandon, quick follow-up for XOi.

A new product plus an acquisition usually expands the in-market list faster than headcount can keep up, and the coverage gap shows up late as a missed quarter. Most teams never map how many meetings they actually need to hit the number.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings XOi needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Brandon, last bit of proof for XOi.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how XOi's reply rate likely compares to other field-service tech vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Brandon, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Launching Advisor and absorbing an acquisition is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a field-service motion? I'll tailor it to XOi either way.
